transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. 

Um... well, they actually sent me here from work. I'm an EMT, and... I hope it's okay if I just explain what happened, I really don't want you to think I'm a problem employee or anything. I was at the station, and I was just organizing the airway bags. I kept moving them into this pattern that I just... I knew was right. And I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud while I did it. 

My lieutenant told me to stop and step away, and... I feel really bad about this, I usually always follow orders, but I wouldn't step away. I couldn't. It just felt like the whole bay would go bad if I broke the sequence. So they told me I needed to come see you. Does... does that make sense?
When you feel that need to organize or repeat things, are there specific unwanted thoughts or images playing in your mind, or is it more just an intense urge to make it feel right?

No, no, it's not like... I don't have bad thoughts or anything like that. I'm a really positive person, usually. I just... it's just this really strong feeling that I have to do it a certain way, or things won't be okay. It's more of an urge, like you said. 

I just want to do a good job, you know? I want everything to be perfect for the next call. I promise I wasn't trying to be difficult with my lieutenant. It just... it felt so important in the moment. Is that... is that a normal thing to feel sometimes?

I really hope you don't think I'm some sort of control freak. I just... I take my job very seriously, because people rely on us, so I want to be perfect there. But everywhere else, I'm just normal. I usually just go with the flow. 

Does that... does that answer your question? I want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Apart from those urges to organize, do you ever experience repetitive, unwanted thoughts or worries that keep popping into your head and won't go away?

No, no, I don't really get anything like that. I don't have, you know, bad thoughts stuck in my head or anything. I'm a pretty upbeat person, honestly. 

I mean, sure, sometimes I worry about doing a good job, but I think everyone does that, right? It's just normal stress from wanting to be a good EMT. But I definitely don't have thoughts that I can't get rid of. I really try to keep a positive mindset. Is that... I mean, that's a good thing, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been experiencing these repetitive routines and the urge to arrange things in this way?

Um, I guess it's been about two months? The, you know, the camera and the paperwork stuff I was doing at the station. I know my behavior got everyone a little alarmed, which I feel really terrible about. I promise I wasn't trying to cause any trouble or make the rest of the crew uncomfortable. I just wanted to be thorough, you know? 

But yeah, it's just been for about the last two months that I've been doing all that. Does that... does that timeline help? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details. I hope I'm explaining it okay.
